claims.statement: For every eligible ordinary-tree instance, the target sum equals dim_Q(K_{p})-dim_Q(K_{p-1}) for the fixed direct sum K_j of relative independence-complex chain spaces indexed by all original favorable leaves.
claims.scope: Finite ordinary trees; x(T)+2<=p; 3p<2alpha(T)+1; F(T,p) exactly the strict original-leaf selector; K_j as defined in the report.
claims.reason: The relative face basis is exactly the independent j-sets of H_v meeting W_v, so its dimension is q_v(j); the contract summand identity then sums to the stated rank difference.

claims.statement: The explicitly defined least-eligible-tag deletion map L:K_p->K_(p-1) is injective for every eligible ordinary-tree instance.
claims.scope: Same lower-region domain and fixed selector as the preceding claim; map L uses original leaf tags, original supports, W_v, and a fixed total order on leaves.
claims.reason: L is well-defined and mixes tags when deletion removes the sole marked neighbor, but no full-rank proof or counterexample was obtained. Injectivity would suffice for the target and is stronger than the target.

limitations: The proposed cross-tag map has no proved universal injectivity property.
A failure of injectivity alone would not refute the primary aggregate.
No exhaustive computation or literature theorem application was performed.
